steps.tx: **New-onset diabetes after transplantation**, termed **NODAT** or **PTDM**, develops in **15%** to **30%** of recipients, primarily driven by **tacrolimus**-induced beta-cell toxicity and **corticosteroid**-induced insulin resistance. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients. Structured clinical management and regular follow-up help guide therapeutic optimization and prevent disease complications.

steps.tx: **Squamous cell carcinoma**, or **SCC**, is the most common **skin cancer** and overall **post-transplant malignancy**, occurring with a **65**- to **250**-fold increased incidence compared to the general population and displaying aggressive biological behavior with high metastatic potential. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

left.title: Early Lesions / Polymorphic PTLD
points: Pathogenesis: Unchecked EBV-driven polyclonal B-cell proliferation
Histology: Heterogeneous lymphoid infiltrate preserving tissue architecture
Primary therapy: 50% reduction of maintenance immunosuppression
Prognosis: High response rate without aggressive chemotherapy

right.title: Monomorphic PTLD (Lymphoma)
points: Pathogenesis: True clonal malignant lymphoma (typically DLBCL)
Histology: Monoclonal sheets of atypical large lymphoid cells
Primary therapy: Rituximab combined with CHOP chemotherapy
Prognosis: Guarded; requires formal oncologic management

steps.tx: **Post-transplant erythrocytosis**, or **PTE**, defined by persistent **hematocrit** exceeding **51%** in men or **48%** in women, develops in **10%** to **15%** of recipients with well-functioning grafts, responding effectively to **ACE inhibitors** or ARBs. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **Transplant renal artery stenosis**, or **TRAS**, develops within **6** to **12** months post-transplant at or near the **arterial anastomosis**, presenting with **refractory hypertension** and an acute rise in serum creatinine upon initiating an ACE inhibitor. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: Primary focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, or **FSGS recurrence**, develops in **30%** to **50%** of first kidney transplants and over **80%** in second grafts, presenting with heavy **nephrotic proteinuria** within hours post-surgery, treatable with urgent **plasma exchange**. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **aHUS recurrence** occurs in **60%** to **80%** of recipients with pathogenic **CFH** mutations. Prophylactic complement **C5 inhibition** with **eculizumab** or ravulizumab successfully prevents thrombotic microangiopathy and allograft loss. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients. Structured clinical management and regular follow-up help guide therapeutic optimization and prevent disease complications.

left.title: CFH Mutation (High Risk)
points: Graft outcome: Preserved allograft survival with C5 blockade

right.title: MCP / CD46 Mutation (Low Risk)
points: Pathology: Membrane-bound regulator expressed on donor endothelium
Prophylaxis: Conservative monitoring without routine C5 inhibitors
Graft outcome: Favorable prognosis with donor MCP expression

steps.tx: A periallograft **lymphocele** occurs in up to **15%** to **20%** of kidney transplants. Collections causing **ureteral compression** or lower extremity edema are definitively managed with laparoscopic **peritoneal fenestration**, termed marsupialization. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: Persistent **tertiary hyperparathyroidism** occurs in **30%** to **50%** of recipients due to autonomous parathyroid hyperplasia, presenting with refractory **hypercalcemia** and hypophosphatemia, managed with **cinacalcet** or subtotal parathyroidectomy. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients. Structured clinical management and regular follow-up help guide therapeutic optimization and prevent disease complications.
